question.question:
For the reporting year a company reports net income of 5900000 USD and declared dividends of 475000 USD on non-convertible preferred shares; weighted-average ordinary shares outstanding are 1950000. Two potential ordinary share instruments were outstanding all year. (1) Options on 160000 shares, exercise price 31.5 USD; the average market price for the year was 39.5 USD. Under the treasury stock method the options count only if the average price strictly exceeds the exercise price; otherwise they add zero incremental shares. (2) Convertible bonds, face value 1200000 USD, annual coupon 8 percent paid in cash and expensed in full, convertible into 360000 ordinary shares in total; the tax rate is 26 percent and the only earnings effect of assumed conversion is the after-tax interest saving. Test instruments sequentially by incremental per-share effect: options first, then the bonds against the EPS figure that already includes the option shares; include the bonds only if their after-tax interest saving per conversion share is strictly less than that EPS figure. Use exact arithmetic and compute diluted earnings per share in USD per share.

Answer format: use exact arithmetic through all intermediate steps, round only the final value half up to 2 decimal digits, and return only the numeric value interpreted in `usd` with no unit label or additional text.

slots.description: Exact basic EPS in USD per share.
Exact treasury-stock incremental shares from options.
After-tax interest saving per conversion share.
Whether the bonds enter diluted EPS.
